title: Phone
description: Brazilian phone numbers: mobile, landline and service numbers.

format.summary: Formats a phone number according to Brazilian phone number patterns.
description: Formats a phone number according to Brazilian patterns.

- Masks (`options`): subscriber number only (`98765-4321`); DDD plus number (`(11) 90000-0000`, 11 digits for a mobile, 10 for a landline); E.164 (`+5511987654321`); international (`+55 11 98765-4321`); service numbers (`0800 123 4567`, `4004-1234`); and an automatic choice among them.
- E.164 and international drop a country code in the input first, as `phone.parse` does.
- Pending decision (findings §2 #4): the reference (JS) defaults to the subscriber-number mask, which truncates a DDD-prefixed number; the other libs default to `(11)99402-9275`.

tests.name: subscriber-number
tests.note: default mask is the 9-digit subscriber number (no DDD); asserted by the reference (JS) unit tests

tests.name: empty
tests.note: several libs return null/None for input they cannot format; the reference returns an empty string

tests.name: ddd-under-default-mask
tests.note: CONTENTIOUS: the reference's default mask ('sn') ignores the DDD and keeps only the first 9 digits (documented and asserted by its tests); other libs format DDD + number, e.g. '(11)3000-0000'

generate.summary: Generates a random, structurally-valid Brazilian phone number (DDD + subscriber number, no formatting/mask applied, see `formatPhone` to format the result).
description: Generates a random Brazilian phone number, unformatted.
- `type`: mobile (DDD + 9 digits starting with 9), landline (DDD + 8 digits starting with 2 to 6) or service (no DDD); omitted, a mobile or a landline at random.

tests.name: generated-is-valid
tests.note: every generated value must pass the lib's own validator

description: Validates a Brazilian phone number, mobile or landline by default.
- A country code (`+55`, `0055` or a bare `55`) is accepted and removed first, as in `phone.parse`.
- `options` can widen or narrow the accepted kinds (mobile, landline, service) and pick the mobile numbering rule of `phone.isValidMobile`.

isValidLandline.summary: Validates if a phone number is a valid Brazilian landline phone.
description: Validates a landline number: DDD plus 8 digits.
- A country code (`+55`, `0055` or a bare `55`) is accepted and removed first, as in `phone.parse`.

isValidMobile.summary: Validates if a phone number is a valid Brazilian mobile phone.
description: Validates a mobile number: DDD plus 9 digits.
- A country code (`+55`, `0055` or a bare `55`) is accepted and removed first, as in `phone.parse`.

- `options` picks the numbering rule: version 1 (default) accepts a first subscriber digit of 6, 7, 8 or 9; version 2 follows Resolução Anatel nº 749/2022, accepts only 7, 8 or 9 and rejects the 700 (satellite) series.

isValidService.summary: Validates if a phone number is a valid Brazilian service number.
description: Validates a Brazilian service number, dialed without a DDD. Only the structure is checked.
- Códigos Não Geográficos `0300`, `0303`, `0500`, `0800` and `0900` followed by 7 digits.
- The abbreviated `300X`/`400X` numbers (8 digits); other carrier prefixes are rejected.
- The 3-digit public utility codes designated by Anatel (e.g. `190`, `192`); `112` and `911` are rejected.

parse.summary: Removes phone formatting characters, returns only digits, and caps the result to 11 digits.
description: Removes phone formatting and keeps only digits, capped to 11 digits.
- A country code (`+55`, `0055` or a bare `55`) is stripped only when 10 or 11 digits are left, so area code 55 is not mistaken for it.

tests.name: ddd-55
tests.note: 11 digits: 55 is read as the DDD, not a country code; asserted by the reference (JS) unit tests
